title: Versioning Docs
Add Askr
text:
0.4.1 is the current release. The public format is askr-html. Quiet Quartz is the visual theme.
quarto add arfiligol/askr@v0.4.1
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: Project Name
  site-url: https://example.github.io/project/

format:
  askr-html:
    toc: true
    toc-title: Sections
    toc-location: right
The installed copy lives at _extensions/arfiligol/askr. Askr does not fetch fonts, icons, or styles from a CDN.
To move to a newer tag, install that tag and render the project again. Commit the updated _extensions copy. Reinstall a reviewed tag instead of editing files inside _extensions/arfiligol/askr.

title: Figures that follow the toggle
text:
A cell can emit a light output and a dark output. Put the light output first:
#| renderings: [light, dark]
With askr-html and theme-toggle, the dark stylesheet carries data-mode="dark", and the toggle adds quarto-dark to body. The Figures page renders a pair of swatches this way.

title: Components
text: Askr restyles native Quarto article components. It does not add new authoring syntax. Each page below is one family, so the current treatment can be reviewed before any further change.

title: Components
text:
Already changed

Headings. Level-two headings no longer draw Quarto’s bottom rule. A divider is an explicit --- instead.
Prose. Article links, highlight, list markers, blockquotes, and the content divider.
Callouts. The five native types, their shell, icons, and disclosure chevron.
Code. Inline code, fenced blocks, and local overflow.
Tables. Header and cell rules.
Mathematics. Display math scrolls inside the measure.
References. In-text citations and the reference list.

title: Components
text:
Still Quarto’s own presentation

Figures and groups. Columns, tabsets, diagrams, and an image from Embla. The groups stay Quarto’s own presentation. The image uses Quarto’s folded Source.
Saved notebook output. A real executed cell, separate from a fenced code block.

Chrome such as Areas, the Page List, and the centered measure is recorded on the Layout page.

title: Askr release plan
text:
This repository owns the askr-html native Quarto HTML extension and its local gallery. Askr is the reading page: measure, type, citations, and callouts. Quiet Quartz remains the visual theme name. The 0.4.1 release targets Quarto 1.10.18. The public format is askr-html. Visual semantics remain CONVERGING until explicit Human acceptance; a version number, merge, or tag does not establish semantic stabilization or deployment.



The extension is self-contained at _extensions/askr and exposes one public format name: askr-html. Its token authority is qdk.scss: documented Quarto Sass variables own color, type, callout color, code, navbar, sidebar, and grid widths, and scss:rules applies the remaining Quartz-derived visuals without importing a Quartz runtime. Schibsted Grotesk (400/700) owns titles and navigation UI; Source Sans 3 (400/600 plus italic) is the locally pinned Source Sans Pro successor used for body text; IBM Plex Mono owns code. Consumers own content, IA, execution, math engine, viewer behavior, privacy, data, and navigation choices. The gallery at this repository root is the source-backed evaluation surface. The shared token authority distinguishes content dividers from quieter layout dividers in each native theme; manual Markdown --- is the opt-in content divider, while sidebar and navigation boundaries use the layout token. Askr is a reusable design-system candidate for direct SCQ-repository adoption. Its layout contract is the theme variables $grid-sidebar-width and $grid-margin-width at 264px, $grid-body-width and $grid-docked-body-width at 630px, and $grid-column-gutter-width at 26px. The root font size is 18px. $sidebar-border is false. One scss:rules track list restates the docked grid from those variables so the 630px measure stays centered; Quarto’s own formula would add 200px to the body and leave the spare space in a right-hand 5fr column. That track rule is the residual coupling to Quarto’s grid line names.



The candidate supplies local fonts/icons, Quartz-on-Quarto light and dark tokens, accessible focus, and native Quarto callout styling. It does not replace Quarto collapse, navigation, highlighting, copying, execution, or rendering runtimes. If the extension cannot be resolved by Quarto, a consumer must fix its extension reference; it must not silently fall back to a remotely hosted asset or a Quartz runtime. Callout type determines color independent of nesting depth. The five Quarto-native types are reproduced within their DOM boundary; Quartz’s additional twelve-family showcase/aliases are not exposed because doing so would require a new authoring syntax transformer or public contract.



No tests are written while this scope is CONVERGING. A merge from develop into main renders this gallery and publishes it to GitHub Pages. Askr does not deploy a consumer’s site. It also does not provide analytics, a separate search engine, graphs, backlinks, hover previews, robots, emoji, consumer APIs, or scientific execution policy. The theme styles Quarto’s native overlay search. A website turns that control on with search.location: navbar and search.type: overlay. This gallery does that.



Render this gallery and a clean consumer that installs the reviewed version tag, including a documented Sass override. Inspect desktop/mobile and light/dark native Quarto behavior, focus, overflow, callout nesting/collapse, navigation, TOC and code-copy. Record factual outcomes in VALIDATION.md; those findings are not Human acceptance gates.



Before a final candidate review, inspect the native Quarto surface in this order: Callout geometry/rhythm (including nested and collapsed forms), Header alignment and toggle visibility, Layout tracks with and without a TOC plus mobile, Divider hierarchy, Typography rhythm, Code surface/overflow/copy, then the combined light/dark system. This checklist is a CONVERGING review aid, not an automated test suite or acceptance gate.

title: Candidate validation receipt
text:
Date: 2026-09-23. Semantic state: CONVERGING. These observations are technical evidence, not Human acceptance thresholds or visual acceptance.



Quarto 1.10.18 rendered the local gallery.
A temporary, isolated Python 3.13 virtual environment supplied Jupyter only for local gallery validation; it is not a repository or extension dependency.
notebooks/simple-output.ipynb was executed by jupyter nbconvert --execute --inplace; its saved output is Saved notebook output: [3, 5, 8] -> 16.
No durable tests, CI configuration, release artifacts, or deployment files were added.




PATH=/tmp/qdk-render-venv/bin:$PATH quarto render .
Succeeded: all gallery pages rendered, including executed notebook-output.qmd; _site/index.html contains #mobile-callout-inspection-target and the rendered output contains the saved notebook result.
The Human-selected Quartz-on-Quarto revision also rendered successfully with the same command: compiled light/dark styles contain the Quartz token values, and the gallery ships local Schibsted Grotesk 400/700 alongside Source Sans 3 body and IBM Plex Mono code faces.
After browser review identified Quarto default-callout specificity leakage, the candidate was rerendered with .callout.callout-style-* shell overrides: compiled CSS confirms the uniform 1px semantic-alpha border, 6.3% semantic shell fill, transparent header, 5px radius, 1rem horizontal shell padding, and Quartz warning #db8942. A browser surface was unavailable to this worker for a replacement screenshot; owner browser review remains the visual receipt.
The gallery’s native titleless/iconless simple callout now renders as title="" plus Quarto’s no-icon DOM class, with no title container; Askr explicitly hides that native no-icon container. Dark navigation surfaces now resolve through --qdk-canvas and --qdk-border; clean-consumer installation and Sass override rendering were rerun successfully.
Nested final children now receive an explicit 1rem bottom margin through a type/appearance-specific selector. Collapsible Quarto headers use .75rem block padding while ordinary headers retain 1rem; title, icon, and chevron are direct flex items with align-self: center. These are authored geometry values verified in compiled CSS and DOM; browser-computed light/dark geometry remains an owner-side visual receipt.
The dark-theme code correction was rerendered in qdk-dark.scss only. Quarto switches theme stylesheets without changing the body class, so its compiled dark-only selectors are intentionally unprefixed: div.sourceCode and source pre resolve to #1f1f22 with a #393639 border and #d4d4d4 plain text. Pandoc comments, keywords/operators, strings/numbers, functions, and builtins/types resolve respectively to #8b949e, #ff7b72, #a5d6ff, #d2a8ff, and #79c0ff. The light stylesheet has no corresponding rules, so the light code palette remains unchanged. Browser-computed values and copy-control icon pixels remain owner-side visual inspection evidence.
The common code-shell rule now assigns the visible border and 5px radius to div.sourceCode (with pre retained as a standalone fallback). For Quarto’s normal nested structure, div.sourceCode > pre.sourceCode and its direct code.sourceCode are explicitly transparent with zero border/radius/shadow; the dark layer applies #393639 only to that outer wrapper. Gallery and clean consumer rendering were rerun after this correction.
The common stylesheet also clears Quarto’s automatic H2 border and bottom padding (including heading pseudo-elements) without depending on the active theme. Explicit hr elements instead render as a 1px top border using --qdk-border; components.qmd demonstrates the opt-in native Markdown sequence of a heading, blank line, and ---. Browser-computed confirmation in both stylesheet modes remains owner-side visual evidence.
The divider hierarchy was rerendered with explicit theme tokens. Light content and layout dividers are respectively rgba(43, 43, 43, .18) and rgba(43, 43, 43, .08); dark values are rgba(212, 212, 212, .24) and rgba(212, 212, 212, .10). The manual hr uses the content token at 1px with opacity: 1; mobile/offcanvas inline-end boundaries stay transparent. The desktop docked sidebar no longer draws a layout-token seam, so the side columns share the article canvas.
The native article-grid defaults now compile from $grid-sidebar-width and $grid-margin-width at 264px, $grid-body-width and $grid-docked-body-width at 630px, and $grid-column-gutter-width at 26px. $sidebar-border is false, so the desktop docked sidebar does not draw a layout seam. Quarto’s docked formula still widens the body by 200px and leaves spare space in a right-hand flexible column, so one qdk.scss rule restates the desktop docked grid from those variables: outer flexible tracks, 264px side columns, 26px gutters, and a 630px measure. #quarto-document-content is a 630px-or-less box with justify-self: center and auto inline margins, so it fills that track and stays centered between the side columns. Navbar rules center the native container and tools as flex items at desktop width; below 992px the collapse keeps Bootstrap’s hidden menu instead of a forced flex row. Links use a 1.25 line-height with .25rem block padding. Article list rhythm is scoped to #quarto-document-content, with the navbar list explicitly reset to zero block margin so Quarto navigation cannot inherit article spacing. Desktop links are .9rem/400 (active 600) against the .98rem/700 brand; mobile links are .85rem. The theme toggle is a 28px control that shows a sun in the light scheme and a moon in the dark scheme, both painted with currentColor. The callout disclosure is a centered chevron in the same color as its title. Post-change browser center/contrast measurements remain owner-side visual evidence.
quarto add <temporary-qdk-extension.zip> --no-prompt
quarto render .
Succeeded in a fresh temporary consumer using examples/consumer-override.yml: its compiled stylesheet contains --qdk-link: #2D5E85; the installed extension contains licenses/Askr-MIT.txt and assets/fonts/SourceSans3VF-Upright.ttf.woff2. The Quartz revision additionally confirmed assets/fonts/SchibstedGrotesk-Regular.woff2 and licenses/Schibsted-Grotesk-OFL.txt. Its rendered CSS resolves those local files relative to the installed extension; no CDN is involved.
Asset SHA-256 values and immutable source URLs/revisions are recorded in ASSET_MANIFEST.md and THIRD_PARTY.md. Quarto output contains both native light/dark stylesheet alternatives and the color-scheme toggle script. The gallery now enables Quarto overlay search (search.location: navbar, search.type: overlay) and the theme styles that control. An earlier gallery receipt left search disabled and rendered no search control or search.json.



The consolidated visual review order is Callout, Header, Layout, Divider, Typography, Code, then final light/dark system behavior. This current pass addresses Callout geometry/rhythm only; the remaining entries must be reviewed as a system after their respective candidate changes settle.
Browser inspection remains required for actual desktop/mobile visual behavior, keyboard focus traversal, collapse/copy interaction, and clipping/overflow. Contrast has not been measured; no acceptance threshold is asserted. The loopback preview is http://127.0.0.1:4568/ (Quarto preview service); a 2026-09-23 loopback curl -I returned HTTP/1.1 200 OK with the gallery title.
Quartz’s full additional callout aliases remain an explicit limitation: the candidate faithfully styles Quarto’s five native types, nesting, and collapse; adding the other Quartz authoring names requires a separate public syntax transformer contract.

title: Credits and attribution
text:
Askr draws substantial visual inspiration from Quartz and adapts selected styling ideas to Quarto; the precise sources and modification record are in the third-party source list.
Quartz supplied design reference rather than a runtime dependency. Schibsted Grotesk, Source Sans 3, and IBM Plex Mono are bundled locally under their SIL Open Font Licenses. Source Sans 3 is the intentional version-pinned Source Sans Pro successor adaptation for body text; Schibsted Grotesk owns titles and navigation UI. Lucide icons are bundled locally under its ISC license and Feather-derived MIT notices. Askr’s own source is MIT licensed; that does not replace any of these third-party terms.

Third-party source list
Bundled asset manifest
Askr MIT license

title: Code
text:
Inline code uses IBM Plex Mono on the highlight token. Fenced blocks keep a transparent fill, a 1px border, and a 5px radius, with padding that leaves the copy control clear of the first line. Copy stays Quarto’s control. Long lines scroll inside the block instead of widening the page.
An inline sample is askr-html.

title: Code
text:
Limits
The theme contains a long source line by scrolling inside the fenced block. Do not wrap a paragraph in a code fence to force a measure; prose belongs in the article, and a fence is for source.

title: References
text:
A knowledge-node page cites the claim in the sentence and keeps the full record at the end. This specimen uses Quarto’s citation syntax. It is not a scientific article, and it does not document an SCQ topic.
A literature review is a selection, not a dump of everything read (Pautasso 2013). Software that produces a result needs a citable identity of its own (Smith et al. 2016). The sentence can name two sources without turning into a bracket list.
The reading measure still comes from the same tools that set type. Knuth’s TeXbook fixes the box model this page inherits (Knuth 1984), Lamport’s manual is the document syntax most scientific pages still assume (Lamport 1994), and Bringhurst states the typographic limits a theme should not invent around (Bringhurst 2004).
Quarto turns @key and [@key] into links when link-citations is set (Posit 2026). Pandoc builds the list and the backlinks (MacFarlane 2026). A long title stays in the list rather than in the heading: the house style manual is cited here, and its full name belongs below (The University of Chicago Press 2017).

title: References
text:
Limits
The theme keeps a long identifier, DOI, or URL inside the measure by allowing it to wrap. It does not restyle the reference list’s hanging indent.
Put a few citations in a sentence, not a cluster in every clause. The list belongs at the end of the page. A heading should name the claim; it should not carry the bibliography.

title: Prose
text:
Article links are weight 600, with no underline. A link inside a paragraph gets a quiet highlight. Hover shifts from the link color to the tertiary color.
A highlighted link sits in a sentence. Strong and emphasis stay in the body face. A marked word is kept visible.

title: Prose
text:
Lists
Markers use the tertiary color.

First unordered item
Second unordered item

Nested item



First ordered step
Second ordered step


Term

A definition stays in the same measure as the paragraph above it.

title: Prose
text:
Quote

The quote rule is a 3px bar in the link color. The text color stays the body color rather than a muted aside.

title: Prose
text:
Divider
Headings do not supply this line. Authors opt in with ---.

The line is 1px, using the content divider token, at full opacity.

title: Prose
text:
Limits
The theme contains a paragraph link and a nested list inside the measure. A paragraph used as a heading, or a list item that is an entire section, should be rewritten as a heading plus a short paragraph.

title: Callouts
text:
The extension maps native Quarto types to a fixed visual meaning: note is muted blue with info, tip is teal with flame, important is lavender with circle alert, warning is amber with triangle alert, and caution is coral with octagon alert. The icons are bundled local Lucide SVGs, exposed as CSS masks rather than a new runtime.
The shell, title, semantic alpha border and fill, 5px radius, icon, and chevron follow Quartz’s callout showcase as closely as Quarto’s DOM permits. Quarto’s five native types, their collapse behavior, and nested callouts are the current interface. Quartz’s additional families and aliases are not invented here.

title: Callouts
text:
The five types






NoteNote



Use note for context that informs but does not interrupt the main thread.








TipTip



Use tip for a helpful practice. The icon remains the flame at all depths.








ImportantImportant



Use important for a material reader decision.








WarningWarning



Use warning when readers should inspect a condition before proceeding.








CautionCaution



Use caution for a concrete risk whose consequence should remain visible.

title: Callouts
text:
Edge cases






NoteA deliberately long custom native title that wraps naturally on a compact phone without changing the callout type



Long custom titles remain part of the native header.








This is a native titleless, iconless simple tip. It is still semantically a tip.









WarningCollapsed native warning





This body is available through Quarto’s own disclosure control. Askr replaces the chevron graphic and keeps the control centered with the title.









CautionExpanded native caution





Minimal appearance continues to be Quarto’s presentation choice, with Askr colors applied to the supported callout DOM.

title: Callouts
text:
Nested callouts






TipPrepare the reader



The teal parent gives a helpful orientation.






ImportantPreserve a decision boundary



The lavender child carries the important condition, rather than inheriting teal.

title: Callouts
text:
Limits
The theme contains a long native title and a nested callout without letting either widen the page. Do not put a table, a figure, and several paragraphs inside one callout; move that material into the article and leave the callout as the warning.

title: Mathematics
text:
Display mathematics may scroll locally. The page width stays the 630px measure.
\[
\mathcal{R}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{\alpha_k\,\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\mu_k)^2}{2\sigma_k^2}\right)}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_k} + \int_0^\infty \frac{\lambda^2 + \omega^2 + \eta^2}{(\lambda + \omega + \eta)^2}\,d\omega.
\]
Inline mathematics stays in the sentence, as in \(\omega_r = 2\pi f\).

title: Mathematics

title: Figures and groups
text:
Theme toggle
Quarto keeps two outputs from one cell and shows one of them. body.quarto-dark hides .light-content; body.quarto-light hides .dark-content. Askr’s dark stylesheet is marked data-mode="dark", so the header toggle adds and removes quarto-dark with the stylesheet.
Emit the light output first, then the dark output:


Source
from IPython.display import HTML, display

def swatch(background, foreground, label):
    display(HTML(
        f'<p style="margin:0;padding:1rem 1.25rem;background:{background};color:{foreground}">{label}</p>'
    ))

swatch("#faf8f8", "#2b2b2b", "Light rendering")
swatch("#161618", "#ebebec", "Dark rendering")


Light rendering


Dark rendering


The same order works for a Plotly figure: draw the light figure, then the dark figure, under #| renderings: [light, dark]. The figure colors are baked into each output. The toggle does not recolor a single picture.

title: Figures and groups

Limits
The theme contains columns, a tabset, and this diagram inside the article width. A figure wider than the measure, or one whose labels are unreadably small, should be redrawn. Do not shrink the type to force a poster into the column.

title: Headings
text: Quarto’s article theme draws a line under h2. Askr removes that rule, including the anchored heading’s pseudo-element, and clears the extra padding. Headings stay Schibsted Grotesk, weight 700, with a tight letter-spacing. The page title above is the level-one sample.

title: Headings
text:
Level two has no underline
This heading is the change. There is no bottom border and no padding reserved for one.

Level three
Used for a step inside a section.

Level four
Used for a smaller break. Levels five and six share this size.

Level five

Level six
A reading break is an ordinary thematic break, not a heading rule.

That rule is the content divider. It is not attached to the heading.

title: Headings
text:
Limits
The theme contains a heading that wraps onto a second line inside the measure. A heading that is really a paragraph should be split: keep the heading short, and put the explanation in the body.

title: Tables
text: The header rule is 2px in the muted token. Body cells use a 1px border in the content border token. A wide table scrolls in its own wrapper.

title: Tables
text:
Limits
The theme contains a wide table and an unbreakable path or SHA-256 inside a cell: the hash may wrap, and extra columns scroll inside the table wrapper. Do not write an essay in a cell. If a cell needs more than one sentence, move that text into the paragraph above the table.

title: Askr
text: Askr is the reading page: measure, type, citations, and callouts. It is a local askr-html extension for complete, long-form reading. It leaves Quarto’s navigation, TOC, callout collapse, highlighting, math, and execution features intact while supplying a restrained typographic and panel system. Quiet Quartz remains the name of this visual theme. How this site arranges Areas, the Page List, and the Section List is recorded on the Layout page.

title: Askr
text:
Reading rhythm
The body face is Source Sans 3, code uses IBM Plex Mono, and CJK text follows the local system fallback sequence. A thin teal link and a lavender quote rule are deliberately quieter than the document itself.






NoteNative Quarto, not a replacement runtime



Askr is presentation only. A consumer continues to own site structure, notebook execution, mathematics, viewer integrations, access control, and data.

title: Askr
text:
Mobile callout inspection target
This section is deliberately concise and narrow-screen friendly. Review it at mobile width to check the header, icon, nested panel, keyboard focus, and local horizontal overflow boundaries. Its stable fragment is #mobile-callout-inspection-target.






TipA teal tip keeps its meaning at every depth





Open this native collapsible tip on desktop and mobile. The type—not nesting depth—owns the teal color.






ImportantA nested lavender important callout



This important notice remains lavender inside a teal tip. Its sentence is intentionally long enough to demonstrate natural wrapping without a page-wide overflow boundary on a compact reading screen.

title: Askr
text:
A reading sample

Keep the page quiet
A design system for documents should make dense evidence easier to read without asking every author to become a frontend specialist. The useful unit is not a hero banner but a paragraph, a source cell, a careful note, and the space between them.
CJK fallback for body text is on the CJK specimen page.
See Components for authoring source and edge cases, then Usage for how a project sets up Askr.

title: Saved notebook output
text:
This page executes a small public arithmetic example during rendering. The same calculation is also saved as notebooks/simple-output.ipynb, whose output was created by executing that notebook locally.
values = [3, 5, 8]
total = sum(values)
print(f"Saved notebook output: {values} -> {total}")

Saved notebook output: [3, 5, 8] -> 16
The output is intentionally simple: it proves an actual notebook-like output surface without importing a scientific workload or making notebook execution a consumer requirement.

title: Layout
text: This site is Askr explaining itself. The names below are the three navigation roles used on these pages.

title: Layout
text:
Areas
The header items are Areas: Gallery, Components, Usage, Credits, and Long list. Choosing an Area switches the Page List. An Area is not a heading inside a page, and it is not repeated as a row of the same pages on the left.

title: Layout
text:
Page List
The left column is titled Pages. Every item is a different page in the current Area. Gallery’s list is this overview’s siblings, including this page. Components lists its own pages, such as the saved notebook output.
Headings inside one page do not belong here.

title: Layout
text:
Section List
The right column is titled Sections. It lists the headings of the current page only. The sections on this page — Areas, Page List, Section List, the reading measure, and RWD — stay on the right.

title: Layout
text:
Reading measure
On a wide desktop the article sits in the center. The reference is a 14-inch laptop at about 50cm: 18px type and a 630px column, about 70 characters a line. A farther screen needs a larger size to keep that same angle. The column grows with the type, so the line does not get shorter. Below 630px the article uses the full window.

title: Layout

RWD
Content type is the article and its headings. UI size is everything else: Area links, the text in both side columns, and icons. The two scales move on their own.

title: Search
text:
Search reads the index of the version you are in. Askr does not add another index, and it does not search across versions.
website:
  search:
    location: navbar
    type: overlay
At 1280px and wider the button sits on the right, immediately left of the theme toggle, and the header stays one row. Below that width it moves to the left.
Render each frozen version with a site-url that includes its directory, so its search.json and result links stay inside that directory:
# the render that is published to /v0.2/
website:
  site-url: https://example.github.io/project/v0.2/
The render copied to / uses the site root, without a version directory. Searching from a v0.2 page then uses /v0.2/search.json only. Version folders and the version menu are set up on Versioning Docs.

title: Tokens
text:
Keep color and type overrides in the project, listed after Askr’s theme:
format:
  askr-html:
    theme:
      light: [default, _extensions/arfiligol/askr/qdk.scss, styles.scss]
      dark: [default, _extensions/arfiligol/askr/qdk.scss, _extensions/arfiligol/askr/qdk-dark.scss, styles.scss]
/*-- scss:rules --*/
:root { --qdk-link: #2D5E85; }
Reinstall a reviewed tag instead of editing _extensions/arfiligol/askr.

title: Areas, the Page List, and Sections
text:
These are three different lists. An Area chooses which Page List is open. The Page List chooses a page. Sections are the headings of that page.








Role
Where it appears
What you put there




Areas
Header
One item per group of pages


Page List
Left column, titled Pages
The pages in the current Area


Sections
Right column, titled Sections
Nothing. Quarto lists the current page’s headings



website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Guide
      - href: reference.qmd
        text: Reference
  sidebar:
    - title: Pages
      style: docked
      contents:
        - text: Overview
          href: index.qmd
        - text: Measure
          href: guide/measure.qmd
    - title: Pages
      style: docked
      contents:
        - text: Overview
          href: reference.qmd
        - text: API
          href: reference/api.qmd
Opening Guide shows the first Page List. Opening Reference shows the second. toc-title: Sections and toc-location: right make the right column. A heading belongs only in Sections, not in the Page List, and not as another Area.
Pages in one Area share a purpose. This Usage area is that kind of split: Add Askr, this page, Versioning Docs, and Search are separate pages because each one is a different job.
This gallery’s Areas are Gallery, Components, Usage, Credits, and Long list. The reading of that split is on the Layout page.
